title: Greek Lemon Chicken and Potatoes
seoTitle: Greek Lemon Chicken and Potatoes | Firefighter Meal
shortDescription: Roast chicken thighs with oregano potatoes and pan jus
subtitle: Roast chicken thighs with oregano potatoes and pan jus
description: Bone-in chicken thighs roast over lemon-garlic potatoes until golden. Pan juices become the finishing sauce at the line.

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Greek Lemon Chicken and Potatoes in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on. Use extra-virgin olive oil as listed — measure each before heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch chicken. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Heat oven and season potatoes
steps.instruction: Heat oven to 425°F. Toss potato wedges with half the oil, oregano, salt, and pepper until evenly coated and lightly glossy on all sides.

steps.title: Arrange chicken over potatoes
steps.instruction: Nest seasoned chicken thighs skin-side up among potatoes on two half-sheets. Tuck lemon wedges and smashed garlic around the pan. Plan about 5 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early. Target 165°F at the thickest point before moving to the next batch.

steps.title: Roast and baste
steps.instruction: Roast 35–40 minutes, basting once with pan juices, until chicken reads 165°F and potato edges turn golden and crisp. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Deglaze pan juices
steps.instruction: Transfer chicken to a holding pan. Add broth to sheet pans, scrape browned bits, simmer on stovetop 2 minutes into a thin jus. Maintain a steady simmer — bubbles should break the surface without a rolling boil that shreds delicate proteins. Hold covered at 140°F up to 20 minutes — log the time if your hall tracks food safety during long shifts. Target 165°F at the thickest point before moving to the next batch.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 165°F. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-service, cover finished food and hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven — never leave proteins below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Note the hold time on the pan with a grease pencil.

steps.title: Portion and open the line
steps.instruction: Portion Greek Lemon Chicken and Potatoes onto sheet trays or hotel pans for family-style service. Stack plates, forks, and napkins at the end of the line so late-arriving crew can self-serve without bottlenecking the cook.

steps.title: Scale for larger halls
steps.instruction: When cooking for more than 8 firefighters, split into two pans halfway through so the bottom layer does not overcook while the top waits — duplicate mise en place if you double batches.

steps.title: Serve with parsley
steps.instruction: Portion chicken and potatoes, spoon jus over top. Potatoes should be tender inside with crisp exterior; chicken skin should crackle lightly.

proTips: Dry chicken skin thoroughly—moist skin never crisps in a hall oven.
Add halved cherry tomatoes last 15 minutes for color and acidity.
Feta crumble at the line adds salt without extra cooking.
tonightSpread: Horiatiki salad with cucumber and tomato.
leftovers: Shred chicken into a lemon-oregano wrap with potatoes.
Chop potatoes into a breakfast hash with eggs.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Sunday-roast energy on a weeknight. Potatoes soak up chicken fat and lemon for maximum flavor per bite.
mealPrepNotes: Par-boil potatoes 8 minutes for extra crisp edges if time allows. Station: Arrange potatoes in a single layer beneath chicken so they fry in rendered fat. Station: Rotate pans and baste chicken with pan juices halfway through roast. Station: Rest tray 5 minutes before portioning so juices redistribute into meat.
